issues.legal_issue: The right of appeal in a suit pending when a replacement rent-control regime came into force remains governed by the appeal provisions preserved for pending proceedings.
material_facts: An ejectment suit was instituted under the earlier rent-control regime and remained pending when a replacement regime came into force.
The tenant applied under the replacement regime for a finding that the suit had abated, and the trial court rejected the application while continuing the suit.

The statutory transition provision required pending suits to be continued and disposed of under the earlier regime, while directing the court to have regard to specified provisions of the replacement regime and preserving the earlier regime’s appeal provisions.
issues.conclusion: The right of appeal concerning the pending suit continued to be governed by the earlier regime’s appeal provisions, even though the court considered the replacement regime’s abatement provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 57(2) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, pending proceedings under the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952, were to continue and be disposed of under the 1952 Act, subject to the stated proviso; the second proviso preserved the 1952 Act’s appeal provisions for proceedings disposed of under it. Thus, applying section 50(2) of the 1958 Act in a pending suit did not change the source of the court’s jurisdiction or the governing appeal provisions.

predicates.pending_rent_proceeding_under_prior_regi: A rent-control proceeding was instituted under an earlier regime and remained pending.
predicates.replacement_regime_takes_effect_during_p: A replacement rent-control regime became applicable while the proceeding was pending.
predicates.transition_preserves_prior_appeal_proces: The transition arrangement continued pending proceedings under the earlier regime and preserved its appeal process for those proceedings.

issues.definition: When a rent-control proceeding remains pending across a change of regime and the transition arrangement preserves the earlier appeal process, that earlier appeal framework governs.

issues.legal_issue: A court’s rejection of a request to record abatement, when it determines only a preliminary issue and the suit continues, is not immediately appealable as a final order.
material_facts: In a pending ejectment suit, the tenant asked the trial court to find that the suit had abated because of the premises’ construction period.
The trial court rejected that request after finding that the tenant had not proved the relevant construction period, and directed that the suit proceed on its merits.
The request raised a preliminary issue about maintainability; the ruling did not decide the parties’ ultimate rights or liabilities.
The tenant’s appeal from the ruling was dismissed as not maintainable, and the Supreme Court held that the ruling could be challenged in an appeal against an eventual decree for eviction.
issues.conclusion: No immediate appeal lay from the trial court’s preliminary finding refusing to record abatement and continuing the suit; the tenant could challenge that finding in an appeal against a decree for eviction, if one was passed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952, did not make every order appealable. Relying on Central Bank of India Ltd. v. Gokal Chand, the Court held that an order must affect a party’s rights or liabilities and that a merely interlocutory finding is not appealable. Ram Charan Das v. Hira Nand was referred to for the distinction that an order dismissing the suit on a finding of abatement would be final, unlike a finding that the suit had not abated and should continue. The tenant’s application was only a request to decide a preliminary issue, not a separate case finally disposed of under section 33; the finding could be challenged in an appeal from the final decree.

rule.if: appeal_from_order_in_pending_ejectment_suit and order_rejects_abatement_request and suit_continues and order_decides_only_preliminary_issue and order_does_not_determine_ultimate_rights

predicates.appeal_from_order_in_pending_ejectment_s: A party seeks to appeal an order made during a pending ejectment suit.
predicates.order_rejects_abatement_request: The trial court rejects a request to find that the suit has abated.
predicates.suit_continues: The trial court directs that the suit proceed to be decided on its merits.
predicates.order_decides_only_preliminary_issue: The order decides only a preliminary issue concerning whether the suit may proceed.
predicates.order_does_not_determine_ultimate_rights: The order leaves the parties’ ultimate rights and liabilities to be decided later.

issues.definition: When an appeal is brought from an order in a pending ejectment suit that rejects an abatement request, continues the suit, and leaves ultimate rights undecided, an immediate appeal is unavailable.
